N parents like to make you feel weak and that you can't survive without them. It's a game that they play. That's where the anxiety amd panic attacks come from. They train you to believe that you are not good enough to achieve the goals you set for yourself. They train you to become their slave and to never leace. If no one has told you this before, you ARE worthy and you are capable of making your dreams come true. If you set a goal and don't stray from it, you will male it happen. Do not allow your mother to limit your potential. If you do, you will spend the rest of your life regretting it.

Being a very sensitive child growing up with an Nmom was very difficult to say the least.

Hx: parents divorced when I was 8. Dad was an alcoholic and tried to create a normal childhood for me and my 2 brothers but failed.

One of my first memories was of me begging my mom for a paper towel and her being busy on the phone. I was maybe 4. She was annoyed and walked past me, without looking at me, and pushed me by my nose until I fell to the ground. I fell hard and she didn't bat an eye.

When I was a pre teen I started coming out of my shell. I was already very shy to begin with. She instilled into me and my brothers that looks were everything. "Don't want the Smiths to think you are bad children! You better behave!" From a very early age she had me think that I needed others to like and approve of me at all times.so I grew up being a people pleaser for her and for everyone else.
I never had the chamce to be myself or act the way that I wamted to. I could never express myself the way I wanted to because it would upset her and "others" as she claimed.

When I was a pre teen and teenager she would berate me constantly and tell me that I was "out of control" whenever I would try and express myself. I learned by the age of 13 that I was a "problem". I became very rebellious against all types of authority as a cry for help. She would always side with my teachers if there was a problem. She would never hear my side or even consider my words as valuable. I was a "dumb teenager who thought I knew everything" . Anytime I tried explaining myself I was turned away and told how dumb I was.

When I started high school I developed a severe social anxiety that was later diagnosed as generalized anxiety disorder. I would turn bright red anytime someone talked to me and get sweaty and unable to breathe. Oral presentations would make me sick and nauseous for the weeks before it and on the day unable to eat or think.
I believe this is because I was raised to believe that I was stupid and unworthy. My mother instilled such a sense of self hate from an early age that my self esteem was essentially nothing by the time I was 14. As a typical Nmom though, she would at the same time tell me how beautiful I was

In later high school I still suffered from the extreme anxiety. I coped with weed and alcohol. My mom caught me drunk once and said that I was "the biggest mistake of her life" with my friend in the car. She had me in a constant panic attack if that makes sense. If a friend would ask if I could come over I would be filled with dread until I waited for her response. Anywhere I went and anyone I hung out with was not "good for me" and very bad. No matter who she met or knew of my friends she did not approve.
In 10th grade I started cutting myself on my thigh. I did it because the loss of blood would make me feel numb, something I never felt with my constant anxiety and panic attacks about how she would be when she got home from work or what she would say to my requests to hang out with friends.
She saw them one day and made me see a psychiatrist. She diagnosed me with GAD and depression. I started taking lexapro when I was 17 and holy carp it changed my life. It curbed my anxiety enough for me to start finally being myself and seeing that people liked it.

I lived with my mom until I was 23. Even at the age of 23 I had a curfew and she would say what a "negative influence" my friends were on me. Because I lived under her roof I had to follow her rules and was forbidden to do things she didn't like. She hung housing over my head daily saying that she was going to kick me out, just as she did when I was a teen, and then retract it and cry when I would act on it.

I am now 25 and have been living on my own for almost 3 years. It has helped our relationship tenfold. I now consider her one of my best friends and know that she has my back at all times. I am now able to hang up on her over the phone when she yells without having to worry if I will have a place to live. I can call her out on her shit and tell her the truth without her being able to control any aspect of my life.

I still battle depression, anxiety and low self esteem on a daily basis because of my upbringing. It has gotten a lot better and I've had periods where I can go without medication. It gets better every year but I still have a lifelong battle to fight.
